original_value: The coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic is putting healthcare systems across the world under unprecedented and increasing pressure according to the World Health Organization (WHO). With the advances in computer algorithms and especially Artificial Intelligence, the detection of this type of virus in the early stages will help in fast recovery and help in releasing the pressure off healthcare systems. In this paper, a GAN with deep transfer learning for coronavirus detection in chest X-ray images is presented. The lack of datasets for COVID-19 especially in chest X-rays images is the main motivation of this scientific study. The main idea is to collect all the possible images for COVID-19 that exists until the writing of this research and use the GAN network to generate more images to help in the detection of this virus from the available X-rays images with the highest accuracy possible. The dataset used in this research was collected from different sources and it is available for researchers to download and use it. The number of images in the collected dataset is 307 images for four different types of classes. The classes are the COVID-19, normal, pneumonia bacterial, and pneumonia virus. Three deep transfer models are selected in this research for investigation. The models are the Alexnet, Googlenet, and Restnet18. Those models are selected for investigation through this research as it contains a small number of layers on their architectures, this will result in reducing the complexity, the consumed memory and the execution time for the proposed model. Three case scenarios are tested through the paper, the first scenario includes four classes from the dataset, while the second scenario includes 3 classes and the third scenario includes two classes. All the scenarios include the COVID-19 class as it is the main target of this research to be detected. In the first scenario, the Googlenet is selected to be the main deep transfer model as it achieves 80.6% in testing accuracy. In the second scenario, the Alexnet is selected to be the main deep transfer model as it achieves 85.2% in testing accuracy, while in the third scenario which includes two classes (COVID-19, and normal), Googlenet is selected to be the main deep transfer model as it achieves 100% in testing accuracy and 99.9% in the validation accuracy. All the performance measurement strengthens the obtained results through the research.

result.paraphrase: The World Health Organization (WHO) says the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic is placing unprecedented and growing strain on healthcare systems worldwide. Advances in computer algorithms, especially Artificial Intelligence, can support early detection of this virus, speeding recovery and easing pressure on healthcare systems. This paper presents a GAN with deep transfer learning for detecting coronavirus in chest X-ray images. The study is driven mainly by the shortage of COVID-19 datasets, particularly for chest X-ray images. Its core approach is to gather every available COVID-19 image up to the time of writing and use a GAN to synthesize additional images, improving detection accuracy from the available X-rays. The dataset used here was assembled from multiple sources and is available for researchers to download and use. It contains 307 images across four classes: COVID-19, normal, bacterial pneumonia, and viral pneumonia. Three deep transfer models are evaluated: AlexNet, GoogLeNet, and ResNet18. They were chosen because their relatively shallow architectures reduce complexity, memory usage, and execution time for the proposed model. The paper tests three scenarios: one with all four classes, a second with three classes, and a third with two classes. In every scenario, the COVID-19 class remains the main target for detection. In the first scenario, GoogLeNet is used as the main deep transfer model, achieving 80.6% testing accuracy. In the second, AlexNet is selected and reaches 85.2% testing accuracy. In the third scenario, which includes only COVID-19 and normal classes, GoogLeNet is chosen again, obtaining 100% testing accuracy and 99.9% validation accuracy. These performance metrics reinforce the study’s results.
